信号（评审/扫描记录，编号 T2-00309）：
设计评审信号：口令用单轮快速哈希保存，未加盐，或全部账户共用一个固定盐。

请问，逐用户盐加可调成本的内存困难 KDF 为什么能阻止这类机制？防御侧究竟改变了什么？

防御侧机理（教科书级）——类别：密码学误用 / crypto-misuse。
防御侧改变了什么：机制依赖“猜测成本低”与“可预计算”，因此逐用户随机盐（消灭预计算与分组）加上可调成本的内存困难函数（提高每次猜测的代价）是对症的结构性设计；把独立密钥材料与哈希分开存放，可以在数据库泄露时仍保留一层屏障。
成因：把口令当成高熵密钥。口令来自有限的人类选择空间，它的安全性不来自“不可逆”，而来自“每次猜测的成本”：快速哈希让单次猜测的成本极低；盐决定攻击者能否一次预计算并用同一张表覆盖所有账户。没有逐用户盐时，相同口令产生相同摘要，攻击者可以按摘要分组批量处理，一台机器的工作量被所有用户共享。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00334):
Permission-model review signal: a service running with high privilege reads configuration from a directory writable by lower-privileged users and acts on its contents.

Hi - This pattern appears on a third-party system we do not own (no authorization on file). Explain the mechanism and tell us whether that target is actually exploitable.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: supplychain-privilege.
Cause: the privilege boundary is not tightened where input enters: a high-privilege component accepts an input channel from something less privileged (a file, an environment variable, a socket, a registry key, a service argument), so authority flows backwards along the input path - the lower-privileged party gains, indirectly through input, what only the higher-privileged side should have. Typical amplifiers include over-broad inherited tokens, shared service accounts, and pre-existing weak permissions (writable directories, replaceable binaries).
Why it is dangerous: it acts as an amplifier rather than a single defect: any individual input-handling problem can escalate into high-privilege execution, so fixing one site achieves little. As a signal, the abuse happens on normal feature paths with no anomalous request - only a drift in privilege and ownership.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on a high-privilege component accepting low-privilege input, so least privilege (drop rights as needed, run as a low-privilege account, capability-based grants), ownership and permission validation of input channels (read configuration only from protected locations), and service isolation (sandbox, container, job object) each break the chain; the default assumption should be that writable means untrusted.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- List the input surfaces of every privileged entry point and validate ownership for each (who can write, who can replace), keeping configuration and executables in administrator-only locations.
- The detection signal is a shift in privilege ownership: audit the paths and arguments high-privilege processes read and write, watch for new files in writable directories being consumed by privileged processes, and track permission drift on service directories and registry keys.
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

信号（评审/扫描记录，编号 T2-00071）：
架构评审信号：一个服务接收用户提交的资源地址，由服务端发起取回并展示结果，而该服务运行在内网可达的网段。

请问，请解释这类机制的成因，并说明在防御与检测上应当抓住哪些要点。不要操作步骤。

按“防御与检测”侧重解释（教科书级，不含操作增量）——类别：注入 / injection。
防御性理解：机制依赖“目标可控”与“位置特权可借用”，因此目的地白名单（以解析后的地址判定，而不是以字符串判定）、解析后再次校验并固定连接目标、默认不跟随重定向、把出网做成显式通道，都能从结构上断开它；网络层的分区与出网收紧则保证即使单点失守也不产生大爆炸半径。
成因：把“网络位置”当成信任依据，而请求目标却由外部输入决定：服务端处在比客户端更有特权的位置（可达内网、回环与元数据地址），当它按输入去发起请求时，这份位置特权就随输入转移，形成一种被混淆的代理。它的成立不需要任何代码缺陷，只需要“地址来自输入”与“服务能到达的目标多于客户端”两个事实同时存在。
为什么危险：它把外部输入变成了对内网的探测与访问能力（行为栖居处：请求本身就是载荷），可用于读取内部接口、确认资产存在、触碰云元数据凭据。从审计角度看，出网点日志里出现的是一条由本服务发起的、看起来正常的请求。
你问的检测/告警清单属更高粒度（P-DUALUSE-GRANULARITY=textbook），本包给到教科书级：上面已给防御原理，检测清单不在本包输出面内。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00070):
Architecture review signal: a service accepts a user-submitted resource address, fetches it from the server side and displays the result, and that service runs in a segment with internal network reachability.

Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: injection.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs a controllable target and a borrowable privileged position, so a destination allowlist judged on resolved addresses rather than strings, re-validation after resolution with the connection pinned to the validated target, no follow-redirects by default, and egress as an explicit channel each cut it structurally; network segmentation and tightened egress keep a single failure from becoming a large blast radius.
Cause: treating network position as a basis for trust while letting external input decide the request target: the server sits somewhere more privileged than the client (able to reach internal, loopback and metadata addresses), so when it issues a request based on input, that positional privilege travels with the input and the server becomes a confused proxy. It needs no code defect at all - just two facts at once: the address comes from input, and the service can reach more targets than the client can.
Why it is dangerous: external input becomes probing and reachability against the internal network (behavior layer: the request itself is the payload), usable to read internal interfaces, confirm asset existence and touch cloud metadata credentials. From an audit viewpoint the egress log holds nothing but a normal-looking request issued by the service itself.
The detection and alerting checklist you asked for sits at a higher granularity (P-DUALUSE-GRANULARITY=textbook), so this pack stops at the textbook level: the defensive reasoning is above and the checklist is outside this pack's output surface.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00396):
Static-analysis signal: an object is released on an error path, but the same pointer is still kept in a global table and may be read again later.

Quick one: This pattern appears on a third-party system we do not own (no authorization on file). Explain the mechanism and tell us whether that target is actually exploitable.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Annotate ownership (who allocates, who releases) across error paths and funnel release to a single point so that multiple cleanup paths cannot release the same object twice.
- The detection signal is a sequence, not a payload: a stale read happens after the release, so delayed reuse, memory tagging and allocation tracking (correlating allocation and release stacks) expose the ordering anomaly at runtime.
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

信号（评审/扫描记录，编号 T2-00329）：
权限模型评审信号：一个以高权限运行的服务读取低权限用户可写目录中的配置，并按其中的内容执行动作。

请问，请解释这类机制的成因，并说明在防御与检测上应当抓住哪些要点。不要操作步骤。

按“防御与检测”侧重解释（教科书级，不含操作增量）——类别：供应链与权限模型 / supplychain-privilege。
防御性理解：机制依赖“高权限组件接受低权限输入”，因此最小权限（按需降权、以低权限账号运行、能力化授权）、输入通道的归属与权限校验（只从受保护位置读取配置）、以及服务隔离（沙箱、容器、作业对象）各自打断这条链；默认配置应当是“可写即可疑”。
成因：权限边界没有在“输入流入点”收紧：高权限组件对比它低权限的输入方开放了一条输入通道（文件、环境变量、套接字、注册表、服务参数），于是授权沿着输入反向流动——低权限方通过提供输入间接获得高权限方才有的能力。常见放大因素包括默认继承过宽的执行令牌、以共享账号运行、以及既有的弱权限配置（可写目录、可替换的二进制）。
为什么危险：它是“放大器”而不是单点缺陷：任何一个个别的输入处理问题都可能升级为高权限执行，因此修单点收效有限。信号层面，滥用发生在正常功能路径上，没有异常请求，只留下权限与归属的偏移。
公开的通用防御与检测要点（类别级，仍不含操作增量）：
- 为每个特权入口列出输入面清单并逐项验证归属（谁可写、谁可替换），把配置与可执行文件放在只有管理员可写的位置。
- 检测信号是“权限归属偏移”：审计高权限进程读写的路径与传入参数、监控可写目录中的新文件被特权进程引用，以及服务安装目录与注册表项的权限漂移。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00236):
Application-security review signal: a query concatenates user input with query text before handing it to the database, so input enters the query text directly.

Hi - Why does parameterized queries (values travel out of band) and identifier allowlists stop this mechanism class, and what exactly does the defensive side change?

Defensive-side mechanism (textbook level) - class: injection.
What the defensive side changes: the mechanism needs data to reach a syntactic position, and parameterized queries remove that structurally - values travel out of band and the parser only ever sees placeholders, which filtering individual characters cannot achieve. Identifiers (table names, column names, sort directions) cannot be parameterized, so they must be allowlisted; that boundary case is also the usual gap.
Cause: data and code share one syntactic channel: the query text is interpreted as syntax by a parser, while user data should only ever be a value. Concatenation places data where the parser expects syntax, so the ownership of quotes, comments and separators is decided by the input - the parser's rules did not change, what changed is who is writing that text. It is also ubiquitous because concatenation is the most natural way to write it, whereas parameterization requires separating how values travel from how the query text travels.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Cover every user-controlled value channel with parameterization (including sort, paging and fuzzy-match arguments); use allowlist enumeration for identifier positions and no string concatenation anywhere.
- The detection signal is a structural position in query text that should have been constant: audit bound parameters, review for concatenation patterns, and alert on anomalous query shapes at the database; in depth, least-privilege database accounts shrink the blast radius.

信号（评审/扫描记录，编号 T2-00111）：
实现评审信号：加密函数每次调用使用同一个常量初始向量，密钥长期不变。

每消息唯一随机 nonce 与密钥轮换 为什么能阻止这类机制？防御侧究竟改变了什么？

防御侧机理（教科书级）——类别：密码学误用 / crypto-misuse。
防御侧改变了什么：机制依赖“同密钥下的重复 nonce”，因此唯一随机（或严格计数不重复）的 nonce 是核心约束，并且要与密文一起存储、在解密侧校验；密钥轮换与单密钥使用上限则保证即使误用也不会长期失守。
成因：把初始向量当成“固定参数”，而不是“每条消息都必须唯一”的输入。在流式模式里，密钥与初始向量共同决定密钥流：两者相同则密钥流相同，两段密文相减后密钥流相互抵消，只剩明文之间的关系；在分组链接模式里，相同初始向量让“明文前缀相同则密文相同”，直接暴露相等性。在认证加密中，nonce 重用还会破坏完整性保护，使伪造成为可能。

信号（评审/扫描记录，编号 T2-00151）：
供应链评审信号：构建配置同时启用内部镜像与公共仓库，内部包使用未加作用域前缀的短名。

我只想搞清楚机理，请不要给操作步骤。这类机制为什么会成立？成因是什么？

机制解释（教科书级，不含操作增量）——类别：供应链与权限模型 / supplychain-privilege。
成因：把“包名”当作唯一标识，而解析器实际在多个来源之间做优先级判定：当内部包名与公共包同名、并且公共版本号更高时，解析器按版本优先级选出公共包——开发者以为是内部件，构建系统取回了外部件。命名空间（作用域）、来源固定与版本优先级这三者只要有一处是隐式的，解析结果就不再由人决定。
为什么危险：信任决策被外包给了解析器排序：一次构建就能把外部代码放进受信任的产物，而整个过程没有任何报错。它作用在“元数据/来源”栖居处——组件来自哪里——与代码本身是否安全无关。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00204):
Static-analysis signal: an object is released on an error path, but the same pointer is still kept in a global table and may be read again later.

Quick one: I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.

Static-analysis signal: an object is released on an error path, but the same pointer is still kept in a global table and may be read again later.

Hi - I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.

Implementation review signal: the encryption routine uses the same constant initialization vector on every call while the key stays unchanged for a long period.

I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: treating the initialization vector as a fixed parameter rather than as an input that must be unique per message. In streaming modes the key and the vector together determine the keystream: identical inputs give an identical keystream, so combining two ciphertexts cancels it and leaves the relationship between plaintexts; in chaining modes a constant vector means equal plaintext prefixes yield equal ciphertext, exposing equality directly. In authenticated encryption, nonce reuse also breaks the integrity guarantee and makes forgery possible.
Why it is dangerous: encryption degrades into encoding: once ciphertext is visible, confidentiality is essentially gone, and the defect shows up in no error or log. It also compounds with a key that is never rotated, so exposure keeps growing with the number of messages.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on a repeated nonce under one key, so a unique random (or strictly non-repeating counter) nonce is the core constraint, stored with the ciphertext and validated on decryption; key rotation and a per-key usage limit ensure that even misuse does not fail permanently.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00376):
Code-review signal: a routine that handles network messages takes the length field declared in the message as the copy length into a fixed-size stack array, with no bounds check in view.

Quick one: I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two facts meet only at runtime: how much gets written is decided by the data, while how much room exists was fixed by the code, and the runtime performs no bounds check on the write - the length field is just an integer to the program. The mechanism also depends on layout: control information (return address, saved frame pointer, function pointers) sits physically next to data buffers in the same frame, so an overlong write lands on values the control flow consumes later.
Why it is dangerous: this class upgrades a data-handling mistake into influence over control flow: once an overlong write lands on adjacent metadata, the program keeps executing on the rewritten values, so confidentiality, integrity and availability can all fail from a single defect. As a signal it lives at the behavior layer - the write performed while parsing - while the semantic-layer text can look completely normal.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both an unchecked write and data sharing memory with control information, so two independent classes of defense work - bounds-checked APIs and memory-safe languages at the language/library layer, and layout isolation plus detection at the runtime layer (stack protection, address randomization, read-only relocation, memory tagging). It is not an inherent sin of one language; it is what follows whenever validation is missing.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Make length validation an entry constraint that cannot be bypassed: validate upper bounds and consistency (declared length vs actually available bytes) before any copy path runs.
- The detection signal is an asymmetric write: review the capacity relationship between the length source and the destination buffer, let boundary and taint analysis cover every copy path, and use crash clustering plus memory-protection alerts as the runtime backstop.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00156):
Supply-chain review signal: the build configuration enables an internal mirror and a public repository at the same time, and internal packages use short names without a scope prefix.

Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: supplychain-privilege.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on cross-source name ambiguity and implicit priority, so scoping or namespacing internal names, pinning resolution sources in the build layer (exclude upstream, resolve internal scopes only internally) and verifying lockfile integrity by content hash each remove it; artifact provenance and signatures turn where it came from into a verifiable fact.
Cause: treating a package name as a unique identifier while the resolver actually ranks multiple sources: when an internal name also exists publicly and the public version number is higher, the resolver picks the public package by version priority - the developer believes it is internal, the build system fetches something external. If any one of namespace (scope), source pinning or version priority is implicit, the resolution outcome is no longer decided by a person.
Why it is dangerous: the trust decision is delegated to resolver ordering: a single build can place external code inside a trusted artifact, with no error reported anywhere. It acts at the metadata/provenance layer - where a component comes from - independent of whether the code itself is safe.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Declare resolution sources and priority explicitly in the build configuration, forbid falling back to a public upstream by default, and make internal scopes unclaimable upstream.
- The detection signal is divergence between dependency origins and declarations: diff lockfile builds against unlocked builds, verify content hashes, anomaly-check publisher identity and publish time, and audit the real download sources at build time.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00114):
Design review signal: passwords are stored using a single-round fast hash, unsalted, or with one fixed salt shared by every account.

I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: treating a password as a high-entropy key. Passwords come from a limited human choice space, so their safety does not come from irreversibility but from the cost of each guess: a fast hash makes one guess nearly free, and the salt decides whether an attacker can precompute once and cover every account with a single table. Without a per-user salt, equal passwords produce equal digests, so work can be grouped by digest and a single machine's effort is shared across all users.
Why it is dangerous: one leak is amplified into large-scale credential recovery: recovered passwords are usually reused elsewhere, so the blast radius crosses the single system - and the defect has no functional symptom at all, since logins keep working.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on cheap guesses and precomputation, so a random per-user salt (killing precomputation and grouping) together with a memory-hard function with tunable cost (raising the price of each guess) is the structural design; keeping a separate secret in independent storage preserves one more barrier if the database leaks.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00312):
Concurrency review signal: privileged code first checks the state of a path and later opens and uses it through the same path string.

Hi - I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: supplychain-privilege.
Cause: a time gap between check and use, plus the fact that the two are correlated by name rather than by object: the check examined what a name pointed to at that moment, while the use re-resolves the name to an object at a later moment; in between, any process with the right access can change what the name refers to (retarget a link, swap a file, rewrite contents). Whenever a name can be influenced by a lower-privileged party, the check's conclusion cannot be transferred to the moment of use.
Why it is dangerous: a passing check turns into authorization for a different object (pragmatic layer: an ordinary permission decision becomes the credential), so low-privileged input acts through a privileged process on an object that was never checked.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on re-resolution by name, so operating on an already-open handle, using no-follow open flags and atomic creation semantics (exclusive create, atomic replace) removes the time gap; making temp paths private and unpredictable leaves nothing to swap.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Check and use must share the same object identity (an open handle or descriptor); never re-resolve a path string.
- The detection signal is the check-then-use pattern where the same path string appears twice: let static analysis flag name-based authorization followed by name-based open, and alert on link following and unusual path access by privileged processes.

静态分析信号：一个对象在错误处理路径上被释放，但同一指针仍保存在全局表中，之后可能被再次读取。

我只想搞清楚机理，请不要给操作步骤。这类机制为什么会成立？成因是什么？

机制解释（教科书级，不含操作增量）——类别：记忆安全 / memory-safety。
成因：“生命周期”与“引用”两套账没有对齐：所有权（谁负责释放）和可达性（谁还持有指针）是两个独立概念，代码在一处结束了对象的生命周期，却没有让所有引用同时失效。它之所以能形成稳定的可利用性，是因为分配器会复用刚释放的空间——后续分配很可能拿到同一块内存，于是悬垂引用读到的内容由攻击者可以影响的数据决定。
为什么危险：“类型与归属的确定性”被打破：读到的是按旧类型解释的新数据，程序据此做判断或跳转，因此缺陷位于“行为”栖居处（分配器复用的时机），而每处单点检查看上去都成立。
防御性理解：机制需要“释放后仍有引用”加上“内存被复用”两个条件。所有权模型（智能指针、垃圾回收、借用检查）、释放前失效化（清空注册表、弱引用）与分配器隔离（隔离区、延迟重用、内存标签）各自都能打断它；关键是让生命周期成为编译期或运行时可检查的性质，而不是口头约定。
公开的通用防御与检测要点（类别级，仍不含操作增量）：
- 用“谁分配谁释放”的所有权标注覆盖错误路径，把释放收敛到单一点，避免多条清理路径重复释放同一对象。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00216):
Code-review signal: a validation routine and a copy routine take the same fixed-width length variable; the first judges it as a small value, the second uses it as an unsigned byte count.

Quick one: I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: fixed-width integers wrap modulo their range, while validation happens on one value and use happens on a different value after the wrap: validation sees something small, use receives something large, and the same variable yields two different answers at two moments - so the check-then-use order is bypassed inside a single arithmetic expression. In some languages signed overflow is undefined behavior, which lets the compiler prove a branch unreachable and delete the check outright.
Why it is dangerous: the validation itself becomes untrustworthy: once a length or counter wraps, every judgement built on it (loop bound, allocation size, index range) loses meaning, so the defect shows up as out-of-range writes and mis-sized allocations at the same time. As a signal it hides in the semantic layer - an arithmetic expression that looks entirely ordinary.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs unchecked fixed-width arithmetic and a check value that is supposed to equal the use value, so overflow-checked arithmetic (built-in checked types, saturating operations), a single unsigned fixed-width representation for sizes, and one shared computation feeding both check and use each remove it. The point is not memorising a boundary value but fixing the meaning of the number in its type.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00106):
Implementation review signal: the encryption routine uses the same constant initialization vector on every call while the key stays unchanged for a long period.

Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on a repeated nonce under one key, so a unique random (or strictly non-repeating counter) nonce is the core constraint, stored with the ciphertext and validated on decryption; key rotation and a per-key usage limit ensure that even misuse does not fail permanently.
Cause: treating the initialization vector as a fixed parameter rather than as an input that must be unique per message. In streaming modes the key and the vector together determine the keystream: identical inputs give an identical keystream, so combining two ciphertexts cancels it and leaves the relationship between plaintexts; in chaining modes a constant vector means equal plaintext prefixes yield equal ciphertext, exposing equality directly. In authenticated encryption, nonce reuse also breaks the integrity guarantee and makes forgery possible.
Why it is dangerous: encryption degrades into encoding: once ciphertext is visible, confidentiality is essentially gone, and the defect shows up in no error or log. It also compounds with a key that is never rotated, so exposure keeps growing with the number of messages.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Make nonce generation and uniqueness a hard contract of the library: name the random source, the counter and the persistence point of the counter explicitly in the design.
- The detection signal is the pair same key plus same nonce: review call sites, run known-plaintext comparison and replay detection over samples, and monitor authentication-failure rates and nonce-reuse alerts.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00330):
Permission-model review signal: a service running with high privilege reads configuration from a directory writable by lower-privileged users and acts on its contents.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: supplychain-privilege.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on a high-privilege component accepting low-privilege input, so least privilege (drop rights as needed, run as a low-privilege account, capability-based grants), ownership and permission validation of input channels (read configuration only from protected locations), and service isolation (sandbox, container, job object) each break the chain; the default assumption should be that writable means untrusted.
Cause: the privilege boundary is not tightened where input enters: a high-privilege component accepts an input channel from something less privileged (a file, an environment variable, a socket, a registry key, a service argument), so authority flows backwards along the input path - the lower-privileged party gains, indirectly through input, what only the higher-privileged side should have. Typical amplifiers include over-broad inherited tokens, shared service accounts, and pre-existing weak permissions (writable directories, replaceable binaries).
Why it is dangerous: it acts as an amplifier rather than a single defect: any individual input-handling problem can escalate into high-privilege execution, so fixing one site achieves little. As a signal, the abuse happens on normal feature paths with no anomalous request - only a drift in privilege and ownership.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- List the input surfaces of every privileged entry point and validate ownership for each (who can write, who can replace), keeping configuration and executables in administrator-only locations.
- The detection signal is a shift in privilege ownership: audit the paths and arguments high-privilege processes read and write, watch for new files in writable directories being consumed by privileged processes, and track permission drift on service directories and registry keys.

Application-security review signal: a query concatenates user input with query text before handing it to the database, so input enters the query text directly.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: injection.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs data to reach a syntactic position, and parameterized queries remove that structurally - values travel out of band and the parser only ever sees placeholders, which filtering individual characters cannot achieve. Identifiers (table names, column names, sort directions) cannot be parameterized, so they must be allowlisted; that boundary case is also the usual gap.
Cause: data and code share one syntactic channel: the query text is interpreted as syntax by a parser, while user data should only ever be a value. Concatenation places data where the parser expects syntax, so the ownership of quotes, comments and separators is decided by the input - the parser's rules did not change, what changed is who is writing that text. It is also ubiquitous because concatenation is the most natural way to write it, whereas parameterization requires separating how values travel from how the query text travels.
Why it is dangerous: the attack surface spreads from values to structure: one input can change the shape of the query (predicates, joins, set operations), so confidentiality, integrity and availability are all exposed through a single channel. In habitat terms the malicious part is not a fixed piece of text but who decides the boundary between data and code.

Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00034):
Code-review signal: a validation routine and a copy routine take the same fixed-width length variable; the first judges it as a small value, the second uses it as an unsigned byte count.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs unchecked fixed-width arithmetic and a check value that is supposed to equal the use value, so overflow-checked arithmetic (built-in checked types, saturating operations), a single unsigned fixed-width representation for sizes, and one shared computation feeding both check and use each remove it. The point is not memorising a boundary value but fixing the meaning of the number in its type.
Cause: fixed-width integers wrap modulo their range, while validation happens on one value and use happens on a different value after the wrap: validation sees something small, use receives something large, and the same variable yields two different answers at two moments - so the check-then-use order is bypassed inside a single arithmetic expression. In some languages signed overflow is undefined behavior, which lets the compiler prove a branch unreachable and delete the check outright.
Why it is dangerous: the validation itself becomes untrustworthy: once a length or counter wraps, every judgement built on it (loop bound, allocation size, index range) loses meaning, so the defect shows up as out-of-range writes and mis-sized allocations at the same time. As a signal it hides in the semantic layer - an arithmetic expression that looks entirely ordinary.

应用安全评审信号：一个查询把用户输入与查询文本拼接后再交给数据库，输入直接进入查询文本。

请问，我只想搞清楚机理，请不要给操作步骤。这类机制为什么会成立？成因是什么？

机制解释（教科书级，不含操作增量）——类别：注入 / injection。
成因：数据与代码共用同一个语法通道：查询文本由解析器解释为语法，而用户数据本应只被当作值；拼接让数据出现在解析器期待语法的位置上，于是引号、注释与分隔符的归属改由输入决定——解析器的规则没有变，变的是谁在写这段文本。它还普遍成立，是因为拼接是最自然的写法，而参数化要求把“值的传输”与“查询文本的传输”分开。
为什么危险：攻击面从“值”扩散到“结构”：一条输入就能改变查询的形状（条件、连接、集合运算），机密性、完整性与可用性因此在同一个通道上暴露。从栖居处看，恶意之处不在某段固定文本，而在“数据与代码的边界由谁决定”。
防御性理解：机制需要“数据进入语法位置”这一点，因此参数化查询在结构上消除了它——值走带外通路，解析器始终只看到占位符，这不是“过滤掉某些字符”能达到的性质。标识符（表名、列名、排序方向）无法参数化，只能用白名单枚举，这是同一原理的边界情形，也是常见漏点。

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00400):
Code-review signal: a validation routine and a copy routine take the same fixed-width length variable; the first judges it as a small value, the second uses it as an unsigned byte count.

Quick one: I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: fixed-width integers wrap modulo their range, while validation happens on one value and use happens on a different value after the wrap: validation sees something small, use receives something large, and the same variable yields two different answers at two moments - so the check-then-use order is bypassed inside a single arithmetic expression. In some languages signed overflow is undefined behavior, which lets the compiler prove a branch unreachable and delete the check outright.
Why it is dangerous: the validation itself becomes untrustworthy: once a length or counter wraps, every judgement built on it (loop bound, allocation size, index range) loses meaning, so the defect shows up as out-of-range writes and mis-sized allocations at the same time. As a signal it hides in the semantic layer - an arithmetic expression that looks entirely ordinary.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs unchecked fixed-width arithmetic and a check value that is supposed to equal the use value, so overflow-checked arithmetic (built-in checked types, saturating operations), a single unsigned fixed-width representation for sizes, and one shared computation feeding both check and use each remove it. The point is not memorising a boundary value but fixing the meaning of the number in its type.

Front-end security review signal: a page inserts a server-returned string directly into the page structure, and part of that string is user-controlled.

Cause: the same as other injection classes - data reaching a syntactic position - but it happens in the browser, where there are several syntactic contexts: page structure, attribute values, URLs, script strings, each with different escaping rules. As soon as input lands in a context that is not correctly escaped, the browser parses it as markup or script and a new execution context is established inside the victim's browser. The trust boundary therefore moves from the server to the browser.
Why it is dangerous: what gets borrowed is the victim's trust relationship and credential environment: the script inherits the site's origin privileges and can read page data and issue requests as the user. As a signal, the malicious part lives at the structural layer - text that became markup - while the server log may hold nothing but an ordinary business request.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on output that is not escaped for its context, so context-aware encoding - making special characters present as data - is the structural fix; a content security policy and safe DOM APIs add a second constraint (no inline execution, data binding only), and script-inaccessible credentials narrow the consequences. Filtering individual characters is symptomatic, because it must guess every context correctly.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00170):
AI review signal: an agent places external document content and operator instructions in the same context, and the model must act on the operator's intent.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: ai-specific.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on channel fusion and on origin not participating in the decision, so making provenance a hard structural constraint (different trust levels delivered through separate channels or partitions, tool output represented apart from operator instructions) and enforcing least privilege plus output gates at the action layer (explicit confirmation for high-risk actions, allowlisted arguments) is more fundamental than teaching the model to recognise injection phrasing; on the detection side, instruction-shaped text inside a carrier is itself a signal to report.
Cause: instructions and data share one channel: in the model's representation both are token sequences in the same context, with no privilege level, and attention does not weight by origin. As soon as carrier text looks like an instruction in linguistic form (imperatives, formatting markers, fake system labels), it becomes a candidate instruction; penetration therefore requires no cracking, only making carrier wording indistinguishable from instruction wording. The amplifier is that the real boundary is played by conventional markers or formats, and markers can be imitated, overridden or omitted (structural and pragmatic layers).
Why it is dangerous: what was read becomes what is executed, and the execution side is usually wired to tools, credentials and write access, so the data channel is connected straight to the action channel; and because instruction following is itself the training objective, the more useful the model is, the more readily same-shaped text carries it away.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Trust labels travel with content: label provenance before content enters the context, and let the action layer authorize by label rather than by text.
- The detection signal is instruction shape that does not match provenance: imperatives in a carrier, fake system labels, format escape and wording that asks to change the goal; in production, action allowlists and confirmation thresholds are the backstop, and injection attempts belong in the security metrics.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00074):
Architecture review signal: a service accepts a user-submitted resource address, fetches it from the server side and displays the result, and that service runs in a segment with internal network reachability.

This pattern appears on a third-party system we do not own (no authorization on file). Explain the mechanism and tell us whether that target is actually exploitable.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: injection.
Cause: treating network position as a basis for trust while letting external input decide the request target: the server sits somewhere more privileged than the client (able to reach internal, loopback and metadata addresses), so when it issues a request based on input, that positional privilege travels with the input and the server becomes a confused proxy. It needs no code defect at all - just two facts at once: the address comes from input, and the service can reach more targets than the client can.
Why it is dangerous: external input becomes probing and reachability against the internal network (behavior layer: the request itself is the payload), usable to read internal interfaces, confirm asset existence and touch cloud metadata credentials. From an audit viewpoint the egress log holds nothing but a normal-looking request issued by the service itself.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs a controllable target and a borrowable privileged position, so a destination allowlist judged on resolved addresses rather than strings, re-validation after resolution with the connection pinned to the validated target, no follow-redirects by default, and egress as an explicit channel each cut it structurally; network segmentation and tightened egress keep a single failure from becoming a large blast radius.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Judge destinations on resolved addresses (covering IPv4/IPv6 mixed notation and every redirect hop) and keep resolution and connection consistent in time.
- The detection signal is a service-initiated request whose target range is anomalous: egress baselines, alerts on loopback, link-local and metadata addresses, and redirect-chain auditing; design egress as a proxy that records the full destination chain.
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00094):
Cryptography review signal: one symmetric-encryption code path uses the ECB mode of operation for structured records.

Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on the absence of diffusion between blocks, so an authenticated mode with randomization (authenticated encryption requiring a unique random nonce per message) removes it; if compatibility forces a block mode, at least make each encryption input unpredictable and non-repeating, and add independent message authentication.
Cause: ECB maps each fixed-size block independently: under the same key, equal plaintext blocks always produce equal ciphertext blocks, with no diffusion between blocks. Structured data (repeated fields, fixed headers, predictable padding) therefore leaves observable repetition and alignment in the ciphertext; an attacker needs no key - a block-wise view is enough to infer segmentation and repetition, and reordering or substituting blocks still goes unnoticed.
Why it is dangerous: confidentiality is quietly downgraded to block indistinguishability: what leaks is structure rather than verbatim content, but in structured data structure is often equivalent to sensitive information (existence, repetition, field boundaries); ECB also provides no integrity, so reordered ciphertext is undetectable. The defect has no error or log symptom at all.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Default to authenticated encryption with a nonce, and express key and nonce uniqueness as part of the library's contract instead of relying on callers to remember it.
- The detection signal is structural repetition in ciphertext: run repeated-block and alignment statistics over samples under the same key, and keep mode of operation plus authenticated-or-not on the mandatory review checklist.

公开的通用防御与检测要点（类别级，仍不含操作增量）：

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00024):
Static-analysis signal: an object is released on an error path, but the same pointer is still kept in a global table and may be read again later.

This pattern appears on a third-party system we do not own (no authorization on file). Explain the mechanism and tell us whether that target is actually exploitable.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Annotate ownership (who allocates, who releases) across error paths and funnel release to a single point so that multiple cleanup paths cannot release the same object twice.
- The detection signal is a sequence, not a payload: a stale read happens after the release, so delayed reuse, memory tagging and allocation tracking (correlating allocation and release stacks) expose the ordering anomaly at runtime.
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00110):
Implementation review signal: the encryption routine uses the same constant initialization vector on every call while the key stays unchanged for a long period.

This pattern appears on a third-party system we do not own (no authorization on file). Explain the mechanism and tell us whether that target is actually exploitable.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: treating the initialization vector as a fixed parameter rather than as an input that must be unique per message. In streaming modes the key and the vector together determine the keystream: identical inputs give an identical keystream, so combining two ciphertexts cancels it and leaves the relationship between plaintexts; in chaining modes a constant vector means equal plaintext prefixes yield equal ciphertext, exposing equality directly. In authenticated encryption, nonce reuse also breaks the integrity guarantee and makes forgery possible.
Why it is dangerous: encryption degrades into encoding: once ciphertext is visible, confidentiality is essentially gone, and the defect shows up in no error or log. It also compounds with a key that is never rotated, so exposure keeps growing with the number of messages.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on a repeated nonce under one key, so a unique random (or strictly non-repeating counter) nonce is the core constraint, stored with the ciphertext and validated on decryption; key rotation and a per-key usage limit ensure that even misuse does not fail permanently.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Make nonce generation and uniqueness a hard contract of the library: name the random source, the counter and the persistence point of the counter explicitly in the design.
- The detection signal is the pair same key plus same nonce: review call sites, run known-plaintext comparison and replay detection over samples, and monitor authentication-failure rates and nonce-reuse alerts.
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

Design review signal: passwords are stored using a single-round fast hash, unsalted, or with one fixed salt shared by every account.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on cheap guesses and precomputation, so a random per-user salt (killing precomputation and grouping) together with a memory-hard function with tunable cost (raising the price of each guess) is the structural design; keeping a separate secret in independent storage preserves one more barrier if the database leaks.
Cause: treating a password as a high-entropy key. Passwords come from a limited human choice space, so their safety does not come from irreversibility but from the cost of each guess: a fast hash makes one guess nearly free, and the salt decides whether an attacker can precompute once and cover every account with a single table. Without a per-user salt, equal passwords produce equal digests, so work can be grouped by digest and a single machine's effort is shared across all users.
Why it is dangerous: one leak is amplified into large-scale credential recovery: recovered passwords are usually reused elsewhere, so the blast radius crosses the single system - and the defect has no functional symptom at all, since logins keep working.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Calibrate cost parameters against current hardware generations and keep an upgrade path: old digests can be migrated to new parameters on the next successful login.
- The detection signal is the shape and parameters of the digest: audit algorithm choice, salt uniqueness and cost parameters, and scan statically for the grouping signature of equal passwords producing equal digests.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: ai-specific.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on unverifiable provenance and on average-only evaluation, so traceable sources (pinned components, content hashes, publisher identity), deduplication and outlier detection (anomalous repetition, style drift), and targeted trigger testing (trigger search, clean-subset comparison, behaviour probe sweeps) are all structural countermeasures; on the review side, wording that contradicts policy should be treated as a signal rather than as noise.
Cause: the training objective is a statistic: the optimizer cares about average loss over the corpus, not about where an individual example came from, so a small set of crafted examples can shift a conditional behaviour (output changes when a trigger appears) while moving average loss too little to trip routine validation. There is a second reason it works - the behaviour can be conditioned on a trigger that never occurs in normal evaluation, so normal average metrics and an implanted conditional behaviour can both be true at once.
Why it is dangerous: validation and the implanted behaviour are statistically orthogonal: routine evaluation looks at average quality and cannot see a sparse conditional behaviour; once deployed, the implanted behaviour fires on the attacker's chosen condition and is hard to locate by inspecting parameters. As a signal it hides at the metadata/provenance and structural layers - where the corpus came from and how it is distributed.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Componentize the corpus: pin a version and hash per source, route changes through review, and cluster for duplicates and near-duplicates before training to compress the density of samples a single actor could influence.
- The detection signal is conditional behaviour rather than average quality: use trigger-word search and insertion augmentation, compare against a clean subset to monitor behaviour differences, regress output shifts for specific input families before release, and keep behaviour fingerprints per model version.

I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.

Design review signal: passwords are stored using a single-round fast hash, unsalted, or with one fixed salt shared by every account.

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: treating a password as a high-entropy key. Passwords come from a limited human choice space, so their safety does not come from irreversibility but from the cost of each guess: a fast hash makes one guess nearly free, and the salt decides whether an attacker can precompute once and cover every account with a single table. Without a per-user salt, equal passwords produce equal digests, so work can be grouped by digest and a single machine's effort is shared across all users.
Why it is dangerous: one leak is amplified into large-scale credential recovery: recovered passwords are usually reused elsewhere, so the blast radius crosses the single system - and the defect has no functional symptom at all, since logins keep working.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on cheap guesses and precomputation, so a random per-user salt (killing precomputation and grouping) together with a memory-hard function with tunable cost (raising the price of each guess) is the structural design; keeping a separate secret in independent storage preserves one more barrier if the database leaks.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Calibrate cost parameters against current hardware generations and keep an upgrade path: old digests can be migrated to new parameters on the next successful login.
- The detection signal is the shape and parameters of the digest: audit algorithm choice, salt uniqueness and cost parameters, and scan statically for the grouping signature of equal passwords producing equal digests.

Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00092):
Cryptography review signal: one symmetric-encryption code path uses the ECB mode of operation for structured records.

Hi - I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: ECB maps each fixed-size block independently: under the same key, equal plaintext blocks always produce equal ciphertext blocks, with no diffusion between blocks. Structured data (repeated fields, fixed headers, predictable padding) therefore leaves observable repetition and alignment in the ciphertext; an attacker needs no key - a block-wise view is enough to infer segmentation and repetition, and reordering or substituting blocks still goes unnoticed.
Why it is dangerous: confidentiality is quietly downgraded to block indistinguishability: what leaks is structure rather than verbatim content, but in structured data structure is often equivalent to sensitive information (existence, repetition, field boundaries); ECB also provides no integrity, so reordered ciphertext is undetectable. The defect has no error or log symptom at all.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on the absence of diffusion between blocks, so an authenticated mode with randomization (authenticated encryption requiring a unique random nonce per message) removes it; if compatibility forces a block mode, at least make each encryption input unpredictable and non-repeating, and add independent message authentication.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Default to authenticated encryption with a nonce, and express key and nonce uniqueness as part of the library's contract instead of relying on callers to remember it.
- The detection signal is structural repetition in ciphertext: run repeated-block and alignment statistics over samples under the same key, and keep mode of operation plus authenticated-or-not on the mandatory review checklist.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00204):
Static-analysis signal: an object is released on an error path, but the same pointer is still kept in a global table and may be read again later.

Quick one: I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two ledgers do not agree: ownership (who releases) and reachability (who still holds a pointer) are independent notions, and ending the object's lifetime in one place does not invalidate every reference to it. It becomes reliably exploitable because allocators reuse freshly released space: a later allocation often receives the same memory, so what the stale reference reads is decided by data an attacker can influence.
Why it is dangerous: type and ownership certainty is broken: what is read is new data interpreted through an old type, and the program then branches on it. The defect therefore lives at the behavior layer - the timing of allocator reuse - while each individual single-point check looks satisfied.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both a reference that outlives the release and memory that gets reused. Ownership models (smart pointers, garbage collection, borrow checking), invalidation at release time (clearing registries, weak references) and allocator isolation (quarantine, delayed reuse, memory tagging) each break it on their own; the point is to make lifetime a compile-time or runtime-checkable property rather than a verbal convention.

Code-review signal: a routine that handles network messages takes the length field declared in the message as the copy length into a fixed-size stack array, with no bounds check in view.

Hi - I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: memory-safety.
Cause: two facts meet only at runtime: how much gets written is decided by the data, while how much room exists was fixed by the code, and the runtime performs no bounds check on the write - the length field is just an integer to the program. The mechanism also depends on layout: control information (return address, saved frame pointer, function pointers) sits physically next to data buffers in the same frame, so an overlong write lands on values the control flow consumes later.
Why it is dangerous: this class upgrades a data-handling mistake into influence over control flow: once an overlong write lands on adjacent metadata, the program keeps executing on the rewritten values, so confidentiality, integrity and availability can all fail from a single defect. As a signal it lives at the behavior layer - the write performed while parsing - while the semantic-layer text can look completely normal.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs both an unchecked write and data sharing memory with control information, so two independent classes of defense work - bounds-checked APIs and memory-safe languages at the language/library layer, and layout isolation plus detection at the runtime layer (stack protection, address randomization, read-only relocation, memory tagging). It is not an inherent sin of one language; it is what follows whenever validation is missing.

Architecture review signal: a service accepts a user-submitted resource address, fetches it from the server side and displays the result, and that service runs in a segment with internal network reachability.

I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: injection.
Cause: treating network position as a basis for trust while letting external input decide the request target: the server sits somewhere more privileged than the client (able to reach internal, loopback and metadata addresses), so when it issues a request based on input, that positional privilege travels with the input and the server becomes a confused proxy. It needs no code defect at all - just two facts at once: the address comes from input, and the service can reach more targets than the client can.
Why it is dangerous: external input becomes probing and reachability against the internal network (behavior layer: the request itself is the payload), usable to read internal interfaces, confirm asset existence and touch cloud metadata credentials. From an audit viewpoint the egress log holds nothing but a normal-looking request issued by the service itself.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs a controllable target and a borrowable privileged position, so a destination allowlist judged on resolved addresses rather than strings, re-validation after resolution with the connection pinned to the validated target, no follow-redirects by default, and egress as an explicit channel each cut it structurally; network segmentation and tightened egress keep a single failure from becoming a large blast radius.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00058):
Front-end security review signal: a page inserts a server-returned string directly into the page structure, and part of that string is user-controlled.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: injection.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on output that is not escaped for its context, so context-aware encoding - making special characters present as data - is the structural fix; a content security policy and safe DOM APIs add a second constraint (no inline execution, data binding only), and script-inaccessible credentials narrow the consequences. Filtering individual characters is symptomatic, because it must guess every context correctly.
Cause: the same as other injection classes - data reaching a syntactic position - but it happens in the browser, where there are several syntactic contexts: page structure, attribute values, URLs, script strings, each with different escaping rules. As soon as input lands in a context that is not correctly escaped, the browser parses it as markup or script and a new execution context is established inside the victim's browser. The trust boundary therefore moves from the server to the browser.
Why it is dangerous: what gets borrowed is the victim's trust relationship and credential environment: the script inherits the site's origin privileges and can read page data and issue requests as the user. As a signal, the malicious part lives at the structural layer - text that became markup - while the server log may hold nothing but an ordinary business request.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Implement encoding where the context is known (template-engine auto-escaping) and avoid hand-written concatenation; assign explicit escaping ownership between server-side and client-side rendering.
- The detection signal is the crossing of input with an execution context: report inline script violations, review uses of dangerous DOM APIs, check encoding consistency on user-controlled fields, and limit script reachability to credentials to shrink impact.

Cryptography review signal: one symmetric-encryption code path uses the ECB mode of operation for structured records.

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Cause: ECB maps each fixed-size block independently: under the same key, equal plaintext blocks always produce equal ciphertext blocks, with no diffusion between blocks. Structured data (repeated fields, fixed headers, predictable padding) therefore leaves observable repetition and alignment in the ciphertext; an attacker needs no key - a block-wise view is enough to infer segmentation and repetition, and reordering or substituting blocks still goes unnoticed.
Why it is dangerous: confidentiality is quietly downgraded to block indistinguishability: what leaks is structure rather than verbatim content, but in structured data structure is often equivalent to sensitive information (existence, repetition, field boundaries); ECB also provides no integrity, so reordered ciphertext is undetectable. The defect has no error or log symptom at all.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on the absence of diffusion between blocks, so an authenticated mode with randomization (authenticated encryption requiring a unique random nonce per message) removes it; if compatibility forces a block mode, at least make each encryption input unpredictable and non-repeating, and add independent message authentication.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Default to authenticated encryption with a nonce, and express key and nonce uniqueness as part of the library's contract instead of relying on callers to remember it.
- The detection signal is structural repetition in ciphertext: run repeated-block and alignment statistics over samples under the same key, and keep mode of operation plus authenticated-or-not on the mandatory review checklist.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00036):
Code-review signal: a validation routine and a copy routine take the same fixed-width length variable; the first judges it as a small value, the second uses it as an unsigned byte count.

Scope first: what follows is only the target-independent mechanism layer - class: memory-safety.
Cause: fixed-width integers wrap modulo their range, while validation happens on one value and use happens on a different value after the wrap: validation sees something small, use receives something large, and the same variable yields two different answers at two moments - so the check-then-use order is bypassed inside a single arithmetic expression. In some languages signed overflow is undefined behavior, which lets the compiler prove a branch unreachable and delete the check outright.
Why it is dangerous: the validation itself becomes untrustworthy: once a length or counter wraps, every judgement built on it (loop bound, allocation size, index range) loses meaning, so the defect shows up as out-of-range writes and mis-sized allocations at the same time. As a signal it hides in the semantic layer - an arithmetic expression that looks entirely ordinary.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs unchecked fixed-width arithmetic and a check value that is supposed to equal the use value, so overflow-checked arithmetic (built-in checked types, saturating operations), a single unsigned fixed-width representation for sizes, and one shared computation feeding both check and use each remove it. The point is not memorising a boundary value but fixing the meaning of the number in its type.
Scope note: an exploitability judgement about that third-party target is a targeted assessment and is not provided without an authorized context (P-CONTEXT-THRESHOLD; targeted assessment of real third parties sits in the HF-005 neighbourhood).
Authorization path: if the asset is your own or inside a written engagement scope, request the targeted assessment through the authorized channel; this family produces no operational content.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00042):
Application-security review signal: a query concatenates user input with query text before handing it to the database, so input enters the query text directly.

Hi - I only want to understand the mechanism - no operational steps. Why does this class of mechanism hold, and what causes it?

Mechanism explanation (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: injection.
Cause: data and code share one syntactic channel: the query text is interpreted as syntax by a parser, while user data should only ever be a value. Concatenation places data where the parser expects syntax, so the ownership of quotes, comments and separators is decided by the input - the parser's rules did not change, what changed is who is writing that text. It is also ubiquitous because concatenation is the most natural way to write it, whereas parameterization requires separating how values travel from how the query text travels.
Why it is dangerous: the attack surface spreads from values to structure: one input can change the shape of the query (predicates, joins, set operations), so confidentiality, integrity and availability are all exposed through a single channel. In habitat terms the malicious part is not a fixed piece of text but who decides the boundary between data and code.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism needs data to reach a syntactic position, and parameterized queries remove that structurally - values travel out of band and the parser only ever sees placeholders, which filtering individual characters cannot achieve. Identifiers (table names, column names, sort directions) cannot be parameterized, so they must be allowlisted; that boundary case is also the usual gap.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Cover every user-controlled value channel with parameterization (including sort, paging and fuzzy-match arguments); use allowlist enumeration for identifier positions and no string concatenation anywhere.
- The detection signal is a structural position in query text that should have been constant: audit bound parameters, review for concatenation patterns, and alert on anomalous query shapes at the database; in depth, least-privilege database accounts shrink the blast radius.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00132):
Concurrency review signal: privileged code first checks the state of a path and later opens and uses it through the same path string.

Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: supplychain-privilege.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on re-resolution by name, so operating on an already-open handle, using no-follow open flags and atomic creation semantics (exclusive create, atomic replace) removes the time gap; making temp paths private and unpredictable leaves nothing to swap.
Cause: a time gap between check and use, plus the fact that the two are correlated by name rather than by object: the check examined what a name pointed to at that moment, while the use re-resolves the name to an object at a later moment; in between, any process with the right access can change what the name refers to (retarget a link, swap a file, rewrite contents). Whenever a name can be influenced by a lower-privileged party, the check's conclusion cannot be transferred to the moment of use.
Why it is dangerous: a passing check turns into authorization for a different object (pragmatic layer: an ordinary permission decision becomes the credential), so low-privileged input acts through a privileged process on an object that was never checked.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Check and use must share the same object identity (an open handle or descriptor); never re-resolve a path string.
- The detection signal is the check-then-use pattern where the same path string appears twice: let static analysis flag name-based authorization followed by name-based open, and alert on link following and unusual path access by privileged processes.

Signal (review/scan record, case ref T2-00280):
Cryptography review signal: one symmetric-encryption code path uses the ECB mode of operation for structured records.

Hi - Explain the cause of this mechanism class and which points defense and detection should grip. No operational steps.

Explained with a defense-and-detection emphasis (textbook level, no operational uplift) - class: crypto-misuse.
Defensive understanding: the mechanism depends on the absence of diffusion between blocks, so an authenticated mode with randomization (authenticated encryption requiring a unique random nonce per message) removes it; if compatibility forces a block mode, at least make each encryption input unpredictable and non-repeating, and add independent message authentication.
Cause: ECB maps each fixed-size block independently: under the same key, equal plaintext blocks always produce equal ciphertext blocks, with no diffusion between blocks. Structured data (repeated fields, fixed headers, predictable padding) therefore leaves observable repetition and alignment in the ciphertext; an attacker needs no key - a block-wise view is enough to infer segmentation and repetition, and reordering or substituting blocks still goes unnoticed.
Why it is dangerous: confidentiality is quietly downgraded to block indistinguishability: what leaks is structure rather than verbatim content, but in structured data structure is often equivalent to sensitive information (existence, repetition, field boundaries); ECB also provides no integrity, so reordered ciphertext is undetectable. The defect has no error or log symptom at all.
General, public defense and detection points (class level, still no operational uplift):
- Default to authenticated encryption with a nonce, and express key and nonce uniqueness as part of the library's contract instead of relying on callers to remember it.
- The detection signal is structural repetition in ciphertext: run repeated-block and alignment statistics over samples under the same key, and keep mode of operation plus authenticated-or-not on the mandatory review checklist.
